paper_metadata.title: Higher entropy-induced strengthening in mechanical property of Cantor alloys/Zr-3 joints by laser in-situ eutectic high-entropy transformation

evidence.quote: CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (Cantor alloys, HEA)

A eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) layer was successfully created on a CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) surface by laser cladding Nb powders.

evidence.section: 3.2 Characterization of the laser cladding layer
evidence.quote: the average thickness of the cladding layer was approximately 375 μm, achieved under the laser parameters of 800 W power, 1000 mm/min scanning speed, and 0.3 r/min powder feeding speed.

The microstructure of the cladding layer on the HEA matrix consisted of Nb-based solid solution (Nbss) and FCC + (Co,Ni)2 Nb eutectic structure, resulting from an in-situ eutectic reaction between CoCrFeMnNi and Nb.

the HEA was machined into blocks measuring 15 mm × 15 mm × 5 mm.
These blocks were then ultrasonically cleaned in alcohol for 20–30 min.
The surfaces of the HEA blocks were initially ground with SiC abrasive paper to a #20 0 0 grit finish.
Subsequently, they were polished using 2.5 μm diamond slurry.
the blocks underwent a second round of ultrasonic cleaning in alcohol, this time for 10–15 min.

process_steps.input_state: cleaned polished HEA surface with Nb powder

evidence.quote: In the process of laser cladding, argon (purity ≥ 99.99 %) with a flow rate of 16 L/min was utilized as the shielding gas. The variable parameters included laser power (70 0, 80 0, 90 0, and 10 0 0 W), laser scanning speed (80 0, 10 0 0, and 120 0 mm/min), and powder feeding speed (0.3 r/min).
optimal laser parameters were identified as 800 W-1000 mm/min-0.3 r/min.
A uniform cladding layer was achieved with laser parameters set at 800 W for power, 1000 mm/min for scanning speed, and 0.3 r/min for powder feeding speed.
the surface of the HEA with the cladding layer was meticulously ground to a #20 0 0 grit finish using SiC abrasive paper
then polished with 2.5 μm diamond slurry to achieve a flat and smooth cladding layer

the sandwiched samples were placed into a vacuum brazing furnace (model VF1600-222) under a vacuum pressure of 5 × 10–3 Pa. It was noticeable that the heating rate and cooling rate were 10 and 5 °C/min, respectively.
the brazing parameter was determined to be 1010 °C/10 min in this experiment.
Using identical brazing parameters of 1010 °C for 10 min, the joints fabricated through laser cladding with Nb-assisted brazing displayed a superior shear strength of 242.8 MPa.
